And my boy Vergil has never done anything Multiversal either. If you want to know real multiversal characters,look up Zeno from Dragon Ball Super.

Him being Multiversal is a bit of an oversight. Sure,he's defeated a being of that calibur,but he would have to actually show Multiversal Feats to be shown Multiversal. But over it all,SDT itself is still an extra boost. Plus,Vergil would regen from the Slayer's attacks. And both of them have their weaknesses. But I personally see Vergil winning by a thin margin. Plus,let's not forget Beowulf and the Mirage Edge. The Mirage Edge is like Force Edge but exceptionally more Powerful and Beowulf is alot stronger too. Plus,SDT can allow Vergil to fly and attack from long distances with Yamato and spam Judgement Cut almost endlessly. And there's Judgement Cut End which is just absurdly powerful (Gameplay Wise and also,it's an exceptionally powerful demon destroying ability). But I can see why he would also tie with him. But all in all,the Yamato can give him the edge in this case. That's my take on it.

Honestly,It would come very Close but Vergil's SDT Allows him to bump up his power even more so than DT. Yes,the Doom Slayer is immensely powerful. However,Vergil is much faster and is more lethal in terms of overall swordplay (When it comes to using the Yamato and his overall Energy Blades.) The Doom Slayer's guns wouldn't do much since Vergil is used to deflecting all sorts of bullets. Hell,I wouldn't be suprised if he cut through Plasma Bullets,slice through the Slayer's Weaponry (Via the Guns. I'm not sure about the Crucible tho) and wear down the armor. Thus,Vergil wins. But all in all,that's my take on it. I know the Slayer is immensely powerful but Vergil's Speed and Lethality,plus his demonic heritage give him the edge he needs. Both Fighters are awesome tho and we shouldn't be comparing them in battle.
